title: Teacher retention × housing × mobility
trigger: Local staff report housing/commute constraints alongside recruitment or retention pressure.
questions: What is measured turnover and by role/experience band?
What share of staff commute across district boundaries and for how long?
What housing-cost indicators are relevant to teacher pay bands?
Could employer-assisted housing, transit, carpooling or schedule changes reduce friction without distorting local housing markets?
caution: Do not treat housing or commute as the sole cause of attrition without local evidence.

title: CTE × employers × colleges × workforce
trigger: Strong local industry demand but weak school-to-work connection.
questions: Which current jobs and long-term occupations are being measured?
Which existing CTE Programs of Study and college certificates align?
What work-based learning can employers safely provide?
What transportation, scheduling and instructor constraints block participation?
caution: Separate current openings from projections and verify individual program availability.

title: Rural specialist capacity × broadband × transport
trigger: Low access to advanced or specialized courses.
questions: Is the constraint teacher availability, schedule, enrollment scale, broadband, transport or equipment?
Can regional teacher-sharing or supervised virtual instruction complement local staff?
Can a library, ESC, college or mobile lab provide supervised infrastructure?
caution: Virtual access is not equivalent to effective access if supervision, devices or bandwidth are inadequate.

title: Learning access × health × attendance
trigger: Attendance or participation barriers with plausible health-service dependencies.
questions: What attendance pattern is measured and at what aggregation?
Are transportation, appointment timing or family-language access interacting with learning time?
caution: Do not infer an individual student's medical condition from attendance or performance data.

title: School continuity × energy × water × food
trigger: Extreme weather, grid, water or supply disruptions threaten learning continuity.
questions: Which critical school loads and water/food functions require continuity?
Which campuses can serve as community learning/resilience nodes?
What backup-power, cooling, safe-water and meal-continuity plans are already funded?
caution: Emergency plans must align with district and local emergency-management procedures.
